questions.q: Why is the Oracle FINPRD instance put into ARCHIVELOG mode as part of standing it up?
options: It retains redo logs after they're recycled, which RMAN needs for point-in-time recovery later in this project
It's required before the listener will start
It makes SQL*Plus queries run faster
It's the default mode for every new Oracle instance and requires no action
questions.explain: ARCHIVELOG mode is what makes RMAN backups and point-in-time recovery possible, which Lesson 93 relies on.

questions.q: Why does every table in MySQL's storefront schema use the InnoDB storage engine instead of MyISAM?
options: The storefront is a transactional workload with concurrent writes, and InnoDB provides row-level locking and crash recovery that MyISAM doesn't
MyISAM has been removed from MySQL 8.0 entirely
InnoDB is required for any table with more than one column
MyISAM only works with PostgreSQL-style schemas
questions.explain: InnoDB's row-level locking and transactional support fit a busy e-commerce checkout workload; MyISAM's table-level locking does not.

questions.q: Which two files govern the PostgreSQL analytics instance's engine settings and client authentication rules?
options: postgresql.conf and pg_hba.conf
my.cnf and listener.ora
tnsnames.ora and sqlnet.ora
pg_dump.conf and pg_basebackup.conf
questions.explain: postgresql.conf holds engine settings, and pg_hba.conf controls host-based client authentication — both covered in Chapter 12.

questions.q: Why is pg_stat_statements enabled on the analytics database during setup in this lesson, rather than waiting?
options: So Lesson 94's performance-tuning work has real accumulated query statistics to examine later
It's required before CREATE DATABASE will succeed
It automatically fixes slow queries as they run
It replaces the need for EXPLAIN ANALYZE entirely
questions.explain: Enabling the extension early means it has been collecting statistics by the time the project reaches performance tuning in Lesson 94.

questions.q: In this project's lab, what environment hosts all three database containers?
options: The Docker-based lab environment introduced in Lesson 5
Three separate physical servers in a data center
A single virtual machine running all three engines natively without containers
A managed cloud database service for each platform
questions.explain: Lesson 91 established that this project runs entirely in the Docker lab from Lesson 5, as the harborline-oracle, harborline-mysql, and harborline-postgres containers.
